title: A full tests.py, stress_test.py or 8-worker gate waits for another one running on the same host
goal: tests.py (full and --changed with more than one worker) and stress_test.py take a host-wide lock (a lock file under the user-independent temp or public directory, holding the pid, clone and start time; a stale holder is cleared) and print who holds it and wait, so sessions sharing a host never run two at once without messaging each other; a test starts two runs and asserts the second waits. Retrospective of SP-z7a5c76b: gates here waited about 40 minutes on cross-session messages for a peer's clean-account run, since parallel full runs had caused random timeouts earlier the same day.
notes: tests.py, stress_test.py and conftest.py hold no host lock, so two sessions' full runs overlap on one host. Raised to P1 by the operator at the SP-5cwekumc retrospective (2026-10-01): four sessions landing in parallel overloaded the host (a land killed for low memory, test timeouts) and a land token had to be passed by hand. A lock wait and hold are recorded as ops host.lock rows once the ops sidecar exists.
